Call a single survival_trans_function element and validate its output

Source: R/validateInputs.R
apply_survival_trans.Rd

assert_survival_trans() only probes each transform once, at a single representative time value, before the prediction grid runs. That catches a transform that is broken everywhere (wrong return type/length, or throws), but not one that only misbehaves away from the probe point – e.g. log(x - 10), which is fine near the probe value but returns NaN once the internal prediction grid (which can range up to 2 * max(observed survival time)) reaches x <= 10. This helper wraps every actual call site inside conditionalYT()/ conditionalYTBio()/conditionalYDT()/conditionalYDTBio() so a bad value is caught immediately, with a clear error, instead of silently corrupting a data.frame column or surfacing later as a cryptic "replacement has ... rows, data has ..." error.

Usage

apply_survival_trans(fun, x, surv_i)
